newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM seeks speedy handover of Pol Pot.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM seeks speedy handover of Pol Pot.

text.p: Cambodia's First Prime Minister said on Thursday he had ordered his top negotiator to meet Khmer Rouge guerrillas holding their former leader Pol Pot and urge them to hand him over to the government quickly.

Prince Norodom Ranariddh said his negotiator travelled to the guerrillas' base at Anlong Veng in northern Cambodia on Thursday to seek a speedy end to the Pol Pot issue, which the prince said was being used against him in his feud with Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.

"Today General Nhiek Bun Chhay travelled to Anlong Veng to solve the problem there and to urge Khieu Samphan to hand Pol Pot to the government quickly," the prince told reporters while on a trip outside the capital.
Khieu Samphan is the political leader of the Khmer Rouge faction which broke with Pol Pot and detained him last month after a violent split among the group's top leaders.
Ranariddh hinted that the powerful Hun Sen might try to use the Khmer Rouge problem as an excuse to attack him and his royalist FUNCINPEC party.
"A group wants to use the Anlong Veng problem for a military attack on FUNCINPEC," the prince said without naming Hun Sen.

The prince was apparently referring to a warning from Hun Sen earlier this week when he threatened to use force if he found Ranariddh's military men bringing Khmer Rouge defectors into the city to boost the strength of the prince's forces.
Ranariddh denied he had any intention of bringing Khmer Rouge defectors into Phnom Penh and said he already had enough troops in the city.
The two prime ministers, who head a deadlocked coalition government, have been waging a bitter struggle for power for more than a year.
The unravelling Khmer Rouge guerrilla group has inflamed their dispute with the two men disagreeing on how to deal with the rebels.

Ranariddh says his main aim is to end the war with the Khmer Rouge and bring peace to the country but he has also said he would be willing to bring Khieu Samphan, and his more moderate Khmer Rouge followers, into his political alliance.
Hun Sen declared any talks with the guerrillas illegal.
The two prime ministers are jockeying for position and trying to bolster their respective political alliances in the run-up to a general election in May.
Tension has been high in Phnom Penh in recent days following numerous reports of troop movements in and around the capital.
Troops loyal to the rival prime ministers clashed north of Phnom Penh on Wednesday though officials played down the fighting.

Ranariddh said the clash was being investigated by a bi-partisan security committee. "It was not a big problem, the security committee is trying to solve it," he said. He said he had no word on casualties.
Military officials said earlier the clash between the two sides followed an argument over an unofficial military road block on a main road north of the city.
Witnesses of the clash said on Thursday the situation was quiet but tense and about 20 soldiers, apparently those involved in the original dispute at the road block, were being detained.
Security sources said both sides had set up checkpoints in recent days to monitor or block their rivals' troop movements.

There have been several tense confrontations at different checkpoints over recent days including two on Thursday involving officials and security men loyal to Ranariddh and troops loyal to Hun Sen, an aide to the prince said.
